title: Subtraction: Cre-on / Flp-off
objective: Explain the subtractive strategy (turn on with Cre, off where Flp is present) and when to use it instead of an AND-gate.

steps.title: Sometimes you want to carve OUT a subset
steps.body: The AND-gate keeps the overlap of two features. The **subtractive** strategy does the opposite for one of them: **turn the payload on with [[Cre]], but off again wherever [[Flp]] is present** ('Cre-on/Flp-off'). You start from a broad Cre population and remove an unwanted slice.

visual.alt: Interactive: switch between AND-gate and subtraction modes, toggle Cre and Flp, and see whether the cell's payload is on.
visual.caption: Switch modes and toggle Cre/Flp — watch when the payload turns on.

steps.prompt: Match the strategy to what it yields.
pairs: Cre cells MINUS the Flp cells
All cells expressing the one marker (leaky)
steps.explanation: Intersection = overlap; subtraction = remove a slice; single Cre = everything the marker hits.

steps.setup: A broad Cre line labels [[DRG]] + nodose neurons. You add a Flp driver active only in nodose neurons, using a Cre-on/Flp-off payload.
options: Both DRG and nodose neurons keep the payload
Only DRG neurons; the nodose cells are subtracted out
Only the nodose neurons retain the payload here
Neither population ends up keeping the payload
steps.reveal: Cre turns it on in both; Flp turns it off in nodose; DRG remains. Subtraction is the right tool when you can define the UNWANTED group more cleanly than the wanted one.

variants.prompt: Cre is on in DRG and nodose; Flp is on only in nodose; the payload is Cre-on/Flp-off. Which neurons keep it?
options: Both DRG and nodose neurons keep the payload
Only DRG neurons; the nodose cells are subtracted out
Only the nodose neurons retain the payload here
Neither population ends up keeping the payload
variants.explanation: Flp-off subtraction removes the Flp+ (nodose) cells, leaving the DRG neurons.

steps.prompt: When is subtraction (Cre-on/Flp-off) a better choice than an AND-gate?
options: When you have a clean marker for the cells you want to exclude
When you have no Flp driver lines available at all
When the reporter signal is simply too dim to see
When your goal is actually to label every cell broadly
steps.explanation: If the unwanted population has the cleaner driver, it's easier to remove it than to positively define the wanted set. Choose the strategy by which group you can target most cleanly.

variants.setup: You're choosing between an AND-gate and Cre-on/Flp-off subtraction.
variants.prompt: When is subtraction the better choice?
options: When you have a clean marker for the cells you want to exclude
When you have no Flp driver lines available at all
When the reporter signal is simply too dim to see
When your goal is actually to label every cell broadly
variants.reveal: Subtraction shines when you can cleanly mark the unwanted population and remove it.
